Choose the bread before comparing the filling

The egg-and-cheese English muffin and homestyle biscuit both list 14 g protein. The biscuit lists 350 kcal against the muffin’s 270: an 80 kcal difference without more listed protein. Carbohydrate changes from 27 g to 33 g, fat from 12 g to 18 g, and sodium from 500 mg to 720 mg.

This comparison is between the complete named sandwiches. It does not isolate the bread’s nutrition, because the published servings are finished recipes, not a controlled bread-only swap.

What changes with bacon or sausage?

For the English muffins in this Canadian guide, bacon lists 330 kcal and 17 g protein; sausage lists 450 kcal and 19 g protein. Choosing sausage adds 120 kcal and 2 g protein relative to the bacon sandwich. It does not follow that the sausage version is higher in every nutrient: sodium is 680 mg versus 710 mg for bacon.

A Farmer’s Wrap is another recipe

The Bacon Farmer’s Wrap is 520 kcal and 19 g protein; the Sausage Farmer’s Wrap is 640 kcal and 21 g protein. Both exceed their named English-muffin counterparts by 190 kcal in this edition. Adding regular fries produces a calculated food total of 810 kcal and 23 g protein. With regular onion rings, it is 680 kcal and 21 g protein. The ring order has 130 fewer kcal, but also 4 g less fibre: 3 g versus 7 g for the complete burger-and-fries calculation.

Your toppings and drink still matter

Four baguettes, four actual recipes

Greggs’ Omelette Breakfast Baguette is 441 kcal and 21 g protein. Bacon is 462 kcal and 26 g protein, sausage is 543 kcal and 24 g protein, and bacon with sausage is 550 kcal and 29 g protein. A filling’s name alone does not predict which complete sandwich has more protein.

The closest calorie pair is not the same protein pair

The omelette and bacon baguettes differ by 21 kcal, while bacon lists 5 g more protein. The sausage baguette is 81 kcal above the bacon version yet lists 2 g less protein. These are finished orders with different amounts and ingredients, not equal servings of bacon, egg and sausage.

articles.title: KFC UK: Fillet Burger, Zinger or a Twister wrap?

articles.question: Is a KFC UK Twister lower in calories than a Fillet Burger?
articles.answer: In the official portions compared here, no: the Fillet Burger lists 463 kcal, while the named Twisters range from 482 to 548 kcal. The wrap’s sauce and full recipe matter.
articles.body_html:
A wrap is not automatically lower in calories

KFC’s UK Fillet Burger lists 463 kcal and 28.8 g protein. All four Twisters shown here list more calories per named item: 482–548 kcal. Their protein values are close to the Fillet Burger’s, ranging from 28.4 to 29.1 g.

Kentucky Mayo Twister1 source-listed item / named size52028.446.1242.6
Supercharger Twister1 source-listed item / named size54829.147.8262.6

What changes between the Twisters?

The Smokey BBQ Twister has 482 kcal, while the Supercharger Twister has 548 kcal: 66 kcal apart. Protein differs by just 0.4 g, from 28.7 to 29.1 g. Fat differs more, from 17.4 to 26 g. If you want a lower-calorie choice among these specific wraps, the sauce recipe matters more than the small protein difference.

Sweet Chilli lists 11 g total sugars; Kentucky Mayo lists 5.1 g. That does not make either sauce a universal “better” choice. Read the whole recipe and the nutrient you care about, rather than treating a sweet or creamy name as a nutrition rule.

Fillet and Zinger are different chicken recipes

The Zinger Burger is 468 kcal and 23 g protein. Its calories are close to the Fillet Burger’s 463 kcal, but protein is 5.8 g lower. A five-calorie gap does not mean the two recipes have identical macros or ingredients.

Salt also differs: 2.2 g for Fillet and 2 g for Zinger, compared with 2.6 g for each Twister in this source. Salt is retained in grams; it is not sodium in milligrams.

Keep a Twister separate from a Twister meal

The official ordering page can present a Twister Wrap Meal, but the nutrition rows used here are the individual wraps. Fries, a drink, a dip or a side salad need their own matching portions. Do not call 520 kcal the total for every Kentucky Mayo Twister meal.

What remains unknown?

The source does not report fibre for these selected rows or a gram weight usable for an equal-weight comparison. We therefore compare the actual named orders and leave fibre unknown. Ingredients, allergies and local availability need the current restaurant information; none is inferred from these calorie totals.

Use the box total, not the per-100 g energy column

Wasabi’s guide supplies both calories per 100 g and calories per portion. Harmony is 620 kcal for its 379 g named portion; Mixed maki is 433 kcal for 266 g; Rainbow is 554 kcal for 365 g. Those values include the dressing in each named full version.

Do not count the dressing twice

The named sandwich’s egg, cheese and meat belong to its finished recipe. Do not add their full values again. The coffee entry is brewed coffee without assumed cream or sugar; flavoured or “plain” iced coffee can be a different sweetened recipe with its own row.

These are calculated combinations, not a promise that a local restaurant sells them as a particular combo or price. No sauce, extra sandwich, modified filling or other drink is included. Source gram weights lack a verified display unit here, so no gram-based serving conversion is invented.
